title: AI-Assisted Narrative Mapping: A Trauma-Informed Framework for Narrative-Based Assessment
abstract: This paper introduces a six-dimensional framework for AI-assisted narrative analysis in psychological assessment, grounded in humanistic and existential psychology. As AI systems become prevalent in daily life, they create new contexts for narrative identity formation and psychological risk, including documented cases of AI-induced dependency, delusional thinking, and social withdrawal. Yet, no existing frameworks integrate narrative psychology, dimensional assessment, and trauma-informed design to address these phenomena. The proposed framework operationalizes assessment across six dimensions: self-awareness (Rogers), emotional processing (Greenberg, Fosha), relational connection (Bowlby, Jordan), purpose and meaning (Frankl, Steger), integration of parts (Schwartz, McAdams), and transcendent/existential alignment (Yalom, Maslow). Each dimension is assessed on a continuum, enabling identification of specific patterns of strength and vulnerability within client narratives. Framework application is demonstrated through a fictionalized composite case in which extended AI interaction preceded delusional beliefs and psychological crisis. The dimensional analysis reveals how narrative themes can illuminate therapeutic targets while honoring the meaning-making functions such narratives serve. A four-stage trauma-informed assessment protocol provides structured clinical methodology. The framework positions AI as an assessment tool augmenting clinical judgment rather than replacing human therapeutic relationships.
